title: The Mystery of Stablecoins, Visa, & Fiserv’s Collapse with Ken Suchoski | The Real Eisman Playbook
summary: Ken Suchoski explains stablecoin reserve economics, cross-border opportunities and the durable advantages of card networks. Eisman focuses on Tether contagion, consumer incentives and preference for Visa/Mastercard. Suchoski favors Circle after its valuation reset and Toast’s restaurant platform, while questioning Fiserv margins and the credit mix at Block. Later disclosures support Circle’s rate sensitivity and Fiserv margin pressure, but Circle’s token-presale revenue complicates apparent operating leverage. The review preserves the guest’s disagreement with Eisman about longer-run benefits from a hypothetical Tether scandal.
assessment: The strongest analysis concerns payment incentives, the distinction between rails and full services, and balance-and-yield economics. The Fiserv margin warning has substantial interim support. Weaknesses include overbroad claims that networks grow without paying distribution partners, insufficiently evidenced comparative compliance assertions, and valuation conclusions that need explicit price horizons. Many numerical examples are teaching illustrations and should not dominate the investment-thesis scorecard.
speaker_map_notes: Ken Suchoski is the guest analyst; Steve Eisman asks questions and explicitly endorses selected mechanisms. Suchoski’s Circle target, Fiserv skepticism and Block/PayPal ratings are guest views. His disagreement over Tether contagion is preserved.
framework_points: Analyze both sides of a payment network, including consumer incentives rather than only merchant fees.
Separate the settlement rail from compliance, local payout, distribution and workflow integration.
Model Circle with reserve balances, yield and partner sharing rather than transaction volume alone.
Distinguish growth in lending earnings from the valuation and capital risks attached to those earnings.
Use per-employee metrics and customer treatment as possible signs of underinvestment, with normalization.
tools_and_charts: Circle reserve return rate, average USDC balance, RLDC and forward EBITDA multiple
Bottom-up stablecoin use-case supply model through 2030
Network contract lengths and fixed-cost break-even share
Fiserv revenue and EBIT per employee versus FIS and Jack Henry
Block gross-profit mix and short-duration lending
transcript_cautions: Published January 26, 2026, but repeated this-year/next-year language and the stock-performance list clearly refer to a 2025 discussion and 2026 outlook; exact recording date is not supplied.
Opening montage repeats later statements; complete discussion ranges are used.
Captions garble Fiserv, Suchoski, EBITDA and cross-border; normalized where context is clear.
The guest corrects Eisman: incumbent cross-border providers, not stablecoins alone, already perform low-cost netting.
USAT and USDT are distinct; the later US launch uses Anchorage Digital Bank as issuer.
Apple Pay free means no additional wallet surcharge in context, not zero card-processing cost.

claims.claim: After a weak period for payment stocks, lower starting valuations improve prospective returns, provided their high returns on capital and growth persist.
claims.speaker: Ken Suchoski
claims.test: Establish whether the stated payments lower valuation proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.qualifications: The retrospective stock-performance list appears to reference 2025, not the January 2026 publication year.
claims.reason: Assume identical future distributable cash flows, dilution and risk. Paying a lower price increases the return implied by those cash flows. This conditional identity does not prove that lower quoted prices leave fundamentals unchanged.
claims.next_check: Re-estimate forward cash flows and risk before interpreting a drawdown as improved value.
